persistence_invariants.brief: A composite UNIQUE constraint on (sku, location) guarantees no two stored records share that pair; a collision is resolved at write time (upsert/reject), never two duplicates. Verify by attempting a second insert of the same (sku, location) against the real branch and asserting the constraint rejects it.
A CHECK constraint enforces quantity >= 0 so stock never goes below zero at write time. Verify an insert/update with a negative quantity is rejected by the DB against the real branch.
sku, location, quantity, and inventory_code are NOT NULL so a stock record cannot persist missing its identifying/quantity data. Verify a null-valued insert is rejected against the real branch.

Each inventory adjustment persists a NOT NULL created_at timestamp and actor that are never updated after write (append-only audit). Verify the row carries a non-null timestamp+actor and that the schema forbids overwriting them, against the real branch.

Each additive Alembic migration is reversible and preserves inventory records created before it (no data loss on upgrade/downgrade). Verify pre-existing rows survive the migration applied to the real branch.

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every additive schema migration with no loss; each inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor. Defended by the migration-reversibility + append-only-audit invariants (PI4, PI5) exercised as real-branch integration tests.

Stock levels never go below zero and never overcommit available quantity; an overcommitting pick is rejected at write time in the service layer, backed by the DB CHECK constraint (PI2). Never a stored negative, never a silent double-allocation.
Every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable by (sku, location); a collision is resolved at write time via the composite UNIQUE constraint (PI1), never two duplicates and never an error page.

Acceptance/integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch. pytest-bdd with Alembic migrations applied to the branch and FK-aware targeted-DELETE cleanup.

The UI is a React + TypeScript single-page application under client/ that navigates client-side with no full-page reloads and applies optimistic in-place row updates reconciled against the server. The backend boundary is a JSON API returning data (renders_via: react), not server-rendered HTML; the client ships its own component tests while the API is covered by the R4 branch integration tests.
Validation errors name the offending field (not a bare 'bad request'), owned at the API boundary. Preference from the NFR brief.
A stock row missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) renders cleanly showing an explicit 'not tracked', never a null crash or blank region. Preference from the NFR brief.
